title: Negotiable Throughput SLA and Dynamic Error-Budgeting Template
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: Produce a negotiable SLA template and operational playbook that ties Dedicated throughput guarantees to a dynamic error-budget calculation and explicit autoscale/fleet controls. The goal is a single, modular contract artifact customers can negotiate (banded throughput commitments, burst allowances, opt-in degraded-mode), together with the implementation checklist and telemetry queries necessary to measure compliance.

Key outcomes: (1) a customer-facing SLA template (plain-language + legal appendix) that includes per-quantile latency/throughput objectives, burst windows, and credit calculation examples; (2) a dynamic error-budget model that calculates credits proportional to shortfall over rolling windows and supports discretionary customer choices (immediate credits vs. degraded-mode acceptance); (3) autoscaler and fleet-control knobs documented for contracts: soft/hard thresholds, cooldowns, pre-emptive provisioning windows, and explicit failover ordering between regions/model-variants; (4) a testing plan and Prometheus/CloudWatch queries to validate measurement and billing integration.

Scope notes: This is specific to Dedicated capacity customers (reserved GPU pools) and feeds into the Dedicated Entitlements and Billing pipeline. It should be compatible with existing credit formulas but introduces a banded, negotiable approach rather than a single flat error-budget. The template will be used by Sales and Legal as the starting point for contract negotiations and by Support/Eng for remediation playbooks.
acceptance_criteria: Customer-facing SLA template (plain English + legal appendix) reviewed by Legal
Error-budget calculator spreadsheet and example scenarios (monthly and 7-day windows) signed off by Finance
Autoscaler policy spec (soft/hard thresholds, cooldowns, pre-provision triggers) created and linked to ENG tickets
Telemetry queries (Prom/CloudWatch) for throughput quantiles and availability are validated in staging and documented
Runbook/update playbook for credit issuance and degraded-mode option is drafted and reviewed by Support
Simulation test demonstrating credit computation on a 24h outage scenario with expected outputs
decisions: Use a two-tier error-budget: baseline window (30d) for long-term commitments and short window (7d) for bursty patterns
Autoscaler exposes soft threshold (start pre-warm) and hard threshold (force burst allocation) with configurable cooldowns per-customer
Credit formula will be proportional to measured capacity shortfall relative to committed throughput for the measurement window with a contract floor to avoid trivial credits
Customers can opt-in to 'degraded-mode' where Redwood routes to a lower-cost model variant during incidents in exchange for reduced or waived credits
Notification policy: 30 min automated alert -> 3 hour escalated notice -> 24 hour customer notification with rollback & credit estimation
